lawyer:
Md Abdul Hai, DAG Arobinda Kumar Roy, AAG ----- For the Petitioner.
Moudud Ahmed with Md Shameem Khaled, Advocates ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Abdul Mazid and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the delay of 3640 days in filing the Revision application should not be condoned and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 11-6-1996 (decree signed on 18-6-1996) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Comilla in Title Appeal No.135 of 1990 preferred a revision application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure before this court, which was out of time by 3640 days, hence the Rule.

3. It is contended in the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act that the impugned judgment and decree was passed on 11-6-1996 (decree signed on 18-6-1996) and the application for certified copy of the said judgment and decree was filed on 5-7-2005 and the same was made ready on 21-7-2005 and the Government pleader took its delivery on 21-9-2005 and the Government pleader after collecting all the relevant papers sent the case record to the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla on 25-9-2005, who sent the file to the Solicitor office on 2-10-2005 which was received on 4-10-2005 and thereafter, the office assistant forwarded the file to the Senior Assistant Secretary on 9-10-2005 and the Senior Assistant Secretary gave his opinion to prefer civil revision on 26-10-2005 and thereafter, the Deputy Solicitor signed the same on 26-10-2005 and then the Solicitor approved the said opinion on 9-11-2005 and thereafter, the file was sent to the office of the Attorney-General on 16-11-2005 which was sent to the learned Deputy Attorney- General, Mr Anamul Haq for drafting revision application on 20-11-2005 and on perusal of the file the learned Deputy Attorney-General found that there has been no explanation of delay from 11-6-1996 to 5-7-2005 and thus, he returned the case file for giving explanation to the Solicitor Wing on 23-1-2006 and thereafter, Solicitor Wing issued a letter on 13-2-2006 to the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla with regard to delay from 11-6-1996 to 5-7-2005, who after collecting explanation from the Government pleader, Comilla sent the same to the Solicitor Wing on 4- 4-2006 and thereafter, Solicitor Wing forwarded the file to the Attorney-General office on 16-4- 2006 and the learned Deputy Attorney-General drafted the same on 23-7-2006 which was typed on 23-7-2006 and filed the case on 4-9-2006 and in the aforesaid manner there has been delay of 3640 days in filing the revision application which may kindly be condoned. It is further contended that with regard to the delay from 11-6-1996 to 5- 7-2005 the Government pleader, Comilla gave explanation stating that. before passing the impugned judgment and decree the case diary and papers were stolen from the iron locker of the Government pleader's office and he informed the matter to the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla. Later on, the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla issued a letter on 26-5-2005 to Government Pleader, Comilla to know about the result of the case and accordingly, he took steps for collecting certified copy of the judgment and decree dated 11-6-1996. It is further contended that there is no gross negligence on the part of the Government- petitioner and the delay has been caused due to the circumstances beyond the control of petitioner, which may kindly be condoned.

4. Mr Md Abdul Hai, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the petitioner has taken me through the application and submits that the delay has been caused in filing the revisional application due to government pleader of Comilla though on a query he gave explanation that before passing the impugned judgment and decree the case diary and papers were stolen from the iron locker of the government pleader's office and thus the government pleader was in dark about the judgment and decree dated 11-6-1996 (decree signed on 18-6-1996), who after receiving a letter issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla on 26-5-2005 came to know about the impugned judgment and decree dated 11-6-1996 and soon thereafter, he filed an application for certified copy of the impugned judgment and decree on 5- 7-2005. He next submits that in the instant case right after getting the letter issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla on 26-5-2005 Government Pleader took prompt action for getting certified copy of the judgment and on getting the same it was also properly forwarded to the Solicitor Wing by the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla and after obtaining approval from the Solicitor Wing the same was forwarded to the learned Attorney-General's Office to prepare the revisional application and to move it before the Court and then the learned Additional Attorney-General concerned endorsed the same to Mr Anamul Haq, Deputy Attorney-General to prepare the case but due to some difficulties he could not prepare the draft and in the meantime there has been a massive change in the setup of the office of the learned Attorney-General and in this way unintentional delay of 3640 days took place in filing the revisional application which may kindly be condoned otherwise, the Government petitioner will suffer irreparable loss. The learned Deputy Attorney- General then relying on two decisions reported in 11 MLR (AD) 42, 10 BLT (AD) 79 submits that it has been laid down by our Supreme Court consistently that for the delay in case of Government agencies it had to be somehow reasonable. No doubt delay of each day has to be explained but each hour's delay need not be meticulously explained unless the Government is found guilty of utter negligence or in action and in the facts and circumstances of the case it is apparent and obvious that the delay did not occur due to gross negligence on the part of the State functionary.

5. Finally, the learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that the instant revision application filed against the judgment of reversal and the petitioner has a good chance of success in the revision application, if the same is heard and disposed of on merit.

6. Mr Moudud Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties, on the other hand, by filing counter affidavit opposes the Rule. Mr Moudud Ahmed in the course of his argument upon placing the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act submits that the proposition of law is by now well settled that in order to get benefit of section 5 of the Limitation Act each day's delay has to be explained by the applicant, be it a private person or the Government and in the instant case the petitioner has miserably failed to explain each day's delay. The learned Advocate drew my attention to the statement of facts made by the petitioner in the petition and submits that judgment and decree passed on 11-6-1996 (decree signed on 18-6- 1996) and the application for certified copy of the said judgment and decree dated 11-6-1995 was filed on 5-7-2005 without any sort of explanation from 11-6-1995 to 5- 7-2005 and the approval was accorded by the Solicitor on 26-10-2005 and the necessary record was received by the learned Attorney-General's Office on 16-4-2006 and immediately it was endorsed to the Deputy Attorney-General to do the needful but admittedly it appears from their statement that till 3-9- 2006 no such revisional application could be prepared by them even though they had knowledge that the Revisional application was barred by limitation more than 10 years.

7. Mr Moudud further submits that no doubt they have stated that the learned Deputy Attorney-General could not prepare the draft due to some difficulty but what stood in the way of the learned Deputy Attorney-General to prepare the revisional application has not been explained.

8. The learned Advocate then submits that admittedly the application was ready for moving before this Court on 4-9-2006 but thereafter also a delay of more than 16 months occurred to file the application for condonation of delay before this Court and no explanation whatsoever has been offered by the petitioner which shows that the petitioner is guilty of inaction or gross negligence in filing the revisional application and the application for condonation of delay before this Court and therefore, this gross negligence on the part of the State functionary cannot be condoned. The learned Advocate relying on the decisions reported in 11 MLR 394, 14 MLR 408, 2 BLC 334 and 6 MLR (AD) 295,47 DLR 244 and 11 BLD 194 submits that in view of the statement of facts made by the petitioner in the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, it is clearly established that they have failed to explain the delay and they are guilty of gross negligence and inaction in preparing and moving the revisional application before this Court.

9. I have perused the application and considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the respective parties. It is true that the Government works through various departments but law is well settled by a number of authorities that the delay must be reasonably explained and the Government stands at par with any other litigant. It has also been laid down in the decisions of our Apex Court as referred to by Mr Moudud Ahmed that Government cannot claim any extra privilege in making an application for condonation of delay and the delay must be explained in a reasonable way though not meticulously. In the instant case even if all the latches are brushed aside the petitioner has failed to explain the delay of more than 3313 days from 11-6-1996 to 5-7-2005 and the delay of more than 16 months which took place for filing an application for con- donation of delay which clearly indicates that in dealing with this case the applicant acted in a gross negligent way which cannot be leniently dealt with. The endorsed Deputy Attorney- General well known that the Revisional application was already barred by limitation but for the reasons best known to him as to why he took more than 16 months for preparing the application for condonation of delay which clearly suggests that the Government officials dealt with the matter in gross negligent and callous manner.

10. Now I like to quote hereunder few lines of the cited decisions for having a better view in the dispute in question.

11. In the case of RAJUK vs Rokeya Begum reported in 6 MLR (AD) 295, it has been held as follows:-

"Aggrieved thereby, the petitioner moved the High Court Division with an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. It was out of time by 1345 days. The inordinate delay was not at all explained. The High Court Division, therefore, by Civil Order No.5551 of 1998 dated 22 November, 1992, summarily rejected it as barred by limitation. The petitioner has now presented this petition for leave to appeal therefrom. Any indulgence regardless of settled principles of law and practice will only give premium to negligence or want of due diligence in public office which is not desirable"

12. In the case of ADC (Rev.) vs Abdul Majid reported in 2 BLC (AD) 11, it has been held as follows:-

The question raised by Mr Chowdhury has already been answered by this Division in the case of Deputy Commissioner vs Kobad Ali, 39 DLR (AD) 205 in the following terms:-

"There is a long practice being followed since the days of Dhaka High Court that a revision- al application is to be filed within the period of ninety days prescribed by law for an appeal, and that the High Court Division may in its discretion entertain an application beyond that period in a suitable case where there is no negligence or laches on the part of the petitioner. This is a long standing practice otherwise sound and reasonable, and it does not call for any departure.

So far as the instant case is concerned the learned Judge of the High Court Division upon assigning cogent reasons has passed the impugned order in exercise of his discretion holding that the petitioner could not give satisfactory explanation for the inordinate delay of 83 days in moving the application in question."

13. In the case of Govt. of Bangladesh, rep- resented by the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet vs Md Makhan reported in 14 MLR 408; it has been held as follows:-

"Thus, the above explanation which is not an explanation of delay day to day basis as such, it is not enough and sufficient explanation within the meaning as contemplated in section 5 of the Limitation Act. The petition filed under section 5 of the Limitation Act itself highlights that the delay took place specially in the office of the Solicitor, Ministry of Law and also in the office of the Attorney General, who are well aware of the consequence of the delay. In this view, it will tantamount to give a premium to such gross latches and reckless conduct, on the part of the concerned officials of the Government if condonation of delay is allowed in such circumstances. The proposition of law is well settled that a litigant whether a Government agency or a private party stands on equal footing in the eye of law.

On consideration of the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, it appears to me that the Government officials did not act bonafide in pursuing its case and there has been gross negligence on the part of the Government and therefore, I am constrained to hold that the way of file has been handled by the office of the Solicitor, Ministry of Law and office of the Attorney General does not create any special circumstances for which some consideration can be extended to consider the causes of delay in filing the revision application."

14. In the case of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Works, Govt. of Bangladesh vs Chairman, Court of Settlement Bangladesh Abandoned buildings, Dhaka and another reported in 1 MLR 294 = 1 BLC 587, it has been held as follows:-

"The learned Assistant Attorney-General drawing our attention to the above quoted paragraph made an attempt to explain the delay. Mere steps are to be taken at different stages of the different agencies or different department of the Government to move this petition at a such inordinate delay does not inspire in us any confidence to condone such delay in absence of any cogent reason not to speak of explaining the delay of each day as held in the pronouncements of a number of cases by the Supreme court. Therefore, neither the submission of Mr Mashuque Hossain Ahmed, Assistant Attorney-General nor the statement explaining the delay as quoted above seems to us to be sufficient cause for not filing this writ petition in time."

15. From a reading of the above quoted decisions, I find a clear view of law as it stands today that a revisional application is to be filed within the period of ninety days prescribed by law for an appeal, and that the High Court Division may in its discretion entertain an application beyond that period in a suitable case where there is no negligence or laches on the part of the petitioner.

16. It is true that concerned authorities of the Government require longer time in making the decision to file Appeal or Revision and then in processing the matter for acting on it and if reasonable explanation of delay in the relevant matter is given, there is no reason why such reasonable explanation of delay should not be accepted.

<u>17. In this case it appears that the Government petitioner having knowledge of the limitation and without sufficient cause slept over the matter years together and allowed the period of limitation to run out. If this sort of negligence is condoned by the Court then the litigant public will be at the mercy of the state functionary since in this application the Government-petitioner has utterly failed to explain the inordinate delay. Court will not help a party who is always sleep over the matter.</u>

18. By the way, it may be observed that having realized the difficulty at the end of the day Mr Arobinda Kumar Roy, the learned Assistant Attorney-General submits that the suit itself is not maintainable inasmuch as admittedly the suit land is a tank and the plaintiff cannot claim any right and title over the tank and under the facts and circumstances of the case the Government petitioner has every chance of success in the instant Revision application if the same is heard and disposed of on merit and, as such, the delay of 3640 days in filing the revision application may kindly be condoned otherwise, the petitioner will suffer irreparable loss resulting in the loss of public.

19. Drawing support for his submissions, the learned Assistant Attorney-General referred to a decision reported in 57 DLR (AD) 120.

20. To this, Mr Moudud Ahmed upon refer- ring the findings of the Court of appeal below submits that the plaintiff to prove his case himself was examined as PW-l, who exhibited his registered deed as Exhibit.2 and the trial Court found long possession of the plaintiff in the suit land though the trial Court dismissed the suit mainly on the ground for non-payment of rent and the court of appeal below rightly reversed the same on the clear finding that non-payment of rent by the tenant is not a ground to draw conclusion that thereby he had lost title, interest and possession of the land. He also submits that the Court of Appeal below as last court of fact on the facts of the case and on consideration of the legal position has also found the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land on the basis of registered kabala deed and inheritance as well and in that view of the matter it can be safely said that there is, in fact, no merit in the revisional application.

21. However, in disposing the Rule on an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, I need not embark upon discussion of the Revisional application on merit.

22. In view of the discussions above, I find no difficulty whatever in holding that the petitioner had acted in a gross negligent way and, as such, there is no scope whatsoever to condone the unexplained delay and if this unexplained inordinate delay of 3640 days is condoned that will only encourage the Government officials to be irresponsible and negligent in their official duties. Thus, I do not find any substance in this Rule.

The rule is, therefore, discharged without any order as to cost. Since the delay of 3640 days is not condoned, the connected Revision application is rejected summarily.

End.
